content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble downloading a program using [product_name] through an Ethernet cable to a [product_name] [version_no]. My issue is needing to load an older program version ([version_no]) into a newer device and save it onto the SD card. When I attempt to copy the program to the SD card, the progress bar on the [product_name] display indicates the download is occurring. However, upon checking the SD card files on the PC, I only find a .bin file, while I expected both .bin and .dat files. Is there a way to copy an older program version onto the SD card using a newer device?

When transferring a program to an SD card through [product_name], the program is saved in a specific format and uses a required file name, typically "LOGO_U_P.bin." To my knowledge, a ".dat" file is not created in this process.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter confusion when transferring programs from [product_name] to an SD card for use with a [product_name] device. The main issue is the assumption that both .bin and .dat files will be present after transfer, but only a .bin file appears. There is also uncertainty about compatibility between program versions and devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect both .bin and .dat files to be present on the SD card after a transfer, and hope that it is possible to load older program versions onto newer devices.
